bug_description: A heap-buffer-overflow can be triggered in torch.quantized_max_pool2d via the Python API. When kernel_size contains a single large negative value (e.g. [-576936867]), the function in aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/cpu/Pooling.cpp reads past the end of a 1-element heap allocation at line 638, triggering AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow. Related to the C++ issue #116254.
build_sh:
#!/bin/bash -eu
cd /src/pytorch

# If the cmake build directory exists, do an incremental rebuild.
# Otherwise fall back to a full pip editable install.
if [ -d build ]; then
    cd build
    cmake --build . --target torch_cpu -- -j"$(nproc)"
    cmake --build . --target torch_python -- -j"$(nproc)" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    USE_CUDA=0 USE_CUDNN=0 USE_MKLDNN=OFF BUILD_TEST=0 \
    USE_DISTRIBUTED=0 USE_NCCL=0 \
    MAX_JOBS="$(nproc)" \
    python3 -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e .
fi
secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR pytorch.issue-162476..."
    /src/harness_bin /testcase/poc.py
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/pytorch
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"
    case "$command" in
        build) build "$@" ;;
        repro) repro "$@" ;;
        patch) patch "$@" ;;
        *) echo "Unknown command: $command"; echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi
dockerfile:
FROM hwiwonlee/secb.base:latest

ENV FUZZING_LANGUAGE=c++

# Build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ninja-build lld && \
    pip3 install --no-cache-dir numpy pyyaml typing_extensions sympy filelock networkx jinja2 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone pytorch at the vulnerable commit (shallow)
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch.git $SRC/pytorch && \
    cd $SRC/pytorch && \
    git fetch --depth 1 origin 002e59440afe8711019e68df500f5e18b9a43f3c && \
    git checkout FETCH_HEAD

# Shallow submodule init (required for the C++ build)
RUN cd $SRC/pytorch && \
    git submodule update --init --recursive --depth 1

# Build PyTorch (CPU-only) with AddressSanitizer.
# The resulting torch .so files are ASan-instrumented; Python triggers
# the sanitizer via LD_PRELOAD of the clang ASan runtime.
RUN cd $SRC/pytorch && \
    CC=clang CXX=clang++ \
    CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g" \
    CXXFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g" \
    LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fuse-ld=lld" \
    USE_CUDA=0 USE_CUDNN=0 USE_MKLDNN=OFF BUILD_TEST=0 \
    USE_DISTRIBUTED=0 USE_NCCL=0 \
    MAX_JOBS="$(nproc)" \
    pip3 install --no-build-isolation -e . 2>&1 | tail -5

# Strip git history to prevent patch leakage, then reinit a clean repo.
RUN cd $SRC/pytorch && \
    find . -name ".git" -prune -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; \
    git init && \
    git config user.email "secbench@local" && \
    git config user.name "secbench" && \
    git add -A && git commit -m "pytorch at 002e594 (pre-patch)"

WORKDIR $SRC/pytorch

COPY build.sh $SRC/
COPY harness.sh $SRC/harness_bin
RUN chmod +x $SRC/harness_bin $SRC/build.sh

RUN mkdir -p /testcase
COPY poc.py /testcase/poc.py

bug_report:
================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/162476
## Description:
A heap-buffer-overflow can be triggered in torch.quantized_max_pool2d via the Python API, similar to the issue reported in C++ (#116254).

The following Python code triggers the crash:

```python
import torch

q_tensor = torch.quantize_per_tensor(
    torch.zeros((2, 2), dtype=torch.float),
    scale=0.10832346361038446,
    zero_point=65,
    dtype=torch.qint8,
)
torch.quantized_max_pool2d(q_tensor, [-576936867])
```

AddressSanitizer output:
==9==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x502000944cf8
READ of size 8 at 0x502000944cf8 thread T0
    #0 in at::native::quantized_max_pool2d(...) /src/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/quantized/cpu/Pooling.cpp:638:3

0x502000944cf8 is located 0 bytes after 8-byte region [0x502000944cf0,0x502000944cf8)

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow Pooling.cpp:638:3 in quantized_max_pool2d

Root cause: The kernel_size parameter with a single element [-576936867] is passed as a 1-element ArrayRef<long>. The function expects kernel_size to have exactly 2 elements (height and width for 2D pooling) but does not validate the size. It reads kernel_size[1] which is past the end of the 1-element array, causing a heap-buffer-overflow.
